meaning: The Indian system of astronomy and astrology; the sidereal calendar, charts and rules this app computes.
The five-limbed almanac of a day: tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana and vara, plus sunrise-based timings.
Lunar day: each 12° of the Moon's gain over the Sun; 30 tithis make a lunar month and they start at any hour.
One of 27 lunar mansions of 13°20' each along the sidereal zodiac; the Moon's nakshatra names the day and the birth star.
Panchang limb from the sum of Sun and Moon longitudes, 27 divisions of 13°20'; distinct from the special day yogas.
Half a tithi; eleven named karanas, of which Vishti (Bhadra) is the one the almanac flags.
The weekday, counted from sunrise to sunrise; its lord (Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn) opens the hora cycle.
Lunar fortnight: Shukla (waxing, new to full Moon) or Krishna (waning, full to new Moon).
The bright fortnight from Amavasya to Purnima, when the Moon waxes.
The dark fortnight from Purnima to Amavasya, when the Moon wanes.
The first tithi of either paksha; Shukla Pratipada opens the lunar month in the Amanta system.
The second tithi of a paksha (Bhai Dooj is Kartik Shukla Dwitiya).
The third tithi of a paksha (Akshaya Tritiya, the three Teej days).
The fourth tithi; Shukla Chaturthi is Vinayaka, Krishna Chaturthi is Sankashti.
The fifth tithi of a paksha (Vasant Panchami, Nag Panchami).
The sixth tithi of a paksha (Chhath, Skanda Shashthi).
The seventh tithi of a paksha (Ratha Saptami).
The eighth tithi of a paksha (Janmashtami, Durga Ashtami, Ahoi Ashtami).
The ninth tithi of a paksha (Rama Navami, Maha Navami).
The tenth tithi of a paksha (Vijaya Dashami).
The eleventh tithi, kept as a fast twice a month; each has its own name (Nirjala, Devshayani, Mokshada...).
The twelfth tithi; the Ekadashi fast is broken (parana) inside it.
The thirteenth tithi; Pradosh is kept when it prevails after sunset, Dhanteras is Kartik Krishna Trayodashi.
The fourteenth tithi; Krishna Chaturdashi at midnight is Shivaratri.
Full-moon tithi, the fifteenth of Shukla paksha; ends the month in the Purnimanta system.
New-moon tithi, the fifteenth of Krishna paksha; ends the month in the Amanta system.
Month reckoning that ends the lunar month at Amavasya; used in the south and west of India.
Month reckoning that ends the lunar month at Purnima; used in the north. Krishna-paksha months carry the next name.
An extra lunar month inserted when a lunation holds no sankranti; it carries no festivals.
A lunar month that holds two sankrantis and is dropped from the sequence; very rare.
A tithi that begins and ends between two sunrises and so touches no sunrise; it is given the day it began.
A tithi that covers two sunrises; most festivals take the first day unless their rule prefers the later one.
A year count. Vikram Samvat (Shaka + 135) and Shaka Samvat both turn on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada here.
The year count used in the north; 57 years ahead of the civil year from Chaitra Shukla Pratipada.
The year count of the Indian national calendar; civil year minus 78 after Chaitra Shukla Pratipada.
The Sun's entry into a sidereal sign; names the solar month and dates festivals like Makar Sankranti.
The Sun's half-year: Uttarayana (northward) or Dakshinayana (southward), sidereal here from Makara and Karka.
The Sun's northward half-year, from the Makara sankranti to the Karka sankranti.
The Sun's southward half-year, from the Karka sankranti to the Makara sankranti.
One of six seasons of two solar months each: Vasanta, Grishma, Varsha, Sharad, Hemanta, Shishira.
Spring season; the Sun in Meena and Mesha (sidereal).
Summer season; the Sun in Vrishabha and Mithuna (sidereal).
Monsoon season; the Sun in Karka and Simha (sidereal).
Autumn season; the Sun in Kanya and Tula (sidereal). Sharad Navratri and Sharad Purnima fall here.
Early winter; the Sun in Vrishchika and Dhanu (sidereal).
Late winter; the Sun in Makara and Kumbha (sidereal).
A 48-minute unit (one thirtieth of a day) and, by extension, a chosen good time for an activity.
The eighth of fifteen daytime muhurtas, centred on local noon; counted as good on every weekday here.
The muhurta 96 to 48 minutes before sunrise, kept for quiet practice.
One eighth of the daytime, placed by weekday, that is avoided for new starts.
A second avoided eighth of the daytime, placed by weekday like Rahu Kaal.
Saturn's portion of the day (also Mandi): an eighth of the daytime placed by weekday and avoided for starts.
Eight equal parts of the day and eight of the night, each named Amrit, Shubh, Labh, Chal, Rog, Kaal or Udveg.
Choghadiya ruled by the Moon; read as good.
Choghadiya ruled by Jupiter; read as good. The word also simply means auspicious.
Choghadiya ruled by Mercury; read as good.
Choghadiya ruled by Venus; read as neutral, suited to movement and travel.
Choghadiya ruled by Mars; read as avoid for new starts.
Choghadiya ruled by Saturn; read as avoid for new starts. Kaal also means time.
Choghadiya ruled by the Sun; read as avoid for new starts.
Planetary hour: twelve equal parts of the day and twelve of the night, lords in Chaldean order from the weekday lord.
The span of the Vishti karana; avoided for new starts when it resides on earth, judged by the Moon's sign.
The seventh karana, also called Bhadra; it recurs eight times a lunar month.
The roughly five days the Moon spends in the last five nakshatras (sidereal 300°-360°, Dhanishtha to Revati).
The direction of travel traditionally avoided on each weekday.
Sunrise; an udaya tithi is the tithi running at sunrise, which names the civil day.
The forenoon, taken as sunrise plus a quarter of the daylight (Vasant Panchami rule).
Midday, taken as sunrise plus half the daylight; Ganesh Chaturthi and Rama Navami are judged here.
The afternoon, taken as sunrise plus seven tenths of the daylight; the time for shraddha, Dussehra and Raksha Bandhan.
The first tenth of the night after sunset; the Trayodashi vrat and the evening lamps of Diwali are judged here.
The middle of the night, about 24 minutes either side of midnight; the time of Shivaratri and Janmashtami.
Dusk or dawn twilight; the Chhath evening arghya is offered at sunset.
Breaking a fast; for Ekadashi it is done in the Dwadashi after Hari Vasara ends, before a fifth of the day passes.
The first quarter of the Dwadashi tithi, during which the Ekadashi fast is not yet broken.
The common Ekadashi reckoning: the day whose sunrise holds the eleventh tithi.
The Ekadashi reckoning that moves the fast a day later when Dashami still runs at dawn.
Without water; the Jyeshtha Shukla Ekadashi traditionally kept without drinking.
A vow or fast kept on a recurring tithi, weekday or festival; the app tracks twelve families.
The Krishna Chaturthi vrat to Ganesha, kept until the Moon rises; on a Tuesday it is Angaraki.
A Sankashti Chaturthi that falls on a Tuesday (Mars's day, Angaraka).
The monthly Shukla Chaturthi vrat to Ganesha, judged at midday.
The monthly Krishna Chaturdashi night vrat to Shiva, judged at nishita.
Setting the kalash that opens Navratri; done while Pratipada runs after sunrise, else in Abhijit.
Nine nights from Shukla Pratipada to Navami in Chaitra and Ashwin, devoted to the goddess.
A water offering, here to the setting and rising Sun during Chhath.
Four-day Sun worship ending on Kartik Shukla Shashthi: Nahay Khay, Kharna, evening arghya, morning arghya.
The first day of Chhath (Chaturthi): a bath and a single plain meal.
The second day of Chhath (Panchami): a day-long fast ending with kheer at dusk.
The Tritiya vrats of the monsoon: Hariyali (Shravana Shukla), Kajari (Bhadrapada Krishna), Hartalika (Bhadrapada Shukla).
The Kartik Krishna Chaturthi fast from sunrise to moonrise.
The Purnima evening vrat and story reading to Vishnu, kept when the full-moon tithi still runs at sunset.
The ancestral rite performed in the afternoon (aparahna) on a death tithi or during Pitru Paksha.
The fortnight of ancestors from Bhadrapada Purnima to Ashwin Amavasya (Purnimanta names), each day matched by tithi.
Sarva Pitru Amavasya, the closing day of Pitru Paksha for all ancestors whose tithi is unknown.
The yearly death anniversary by tithi (not civil date), observed in the afternoon.
The tithi running at the moment of birth; its yearly return is the traditional birthday.
A good day yoga from a weekday meeting a matching nakshatra (for example Sunday with Hasta).
A good day yoga from a weekday meeting one of its listed nakshatras.
Pushya nakshatra on a Sunday; a day favoured for starts and purchases.
Pushya nakshatra on a Thursday; a day favoured for starts and purchases.
A Sunday, Tuesday or Saturday meeting a bhadra tithi (2, 7, 12) and one of six nakshatras; events are said to repeat threefold.
Like Tripushkar but with Mrigashira, Chitra or Dhanishtha; events are said to repeat twofold.
The Moon's nakshatra 4th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 13th or 20th from the Sun's; counted as supportive.
The birth chart: planets placed in the twelve signs and houses for the birth moment and place.
The ascendant: the sign rising in the east at birth, which becomes the first house.
The main chart with houses counted from the Lagna (whole-sign houses here).
The Moon chart: houses counted from the Moon's sign; used alone when the birth time is unknown.
A zodiac sign of 30°, twelve from Mesha to Meena, measured sidereally with the chosen ayanamsa.
The Moon sign at birth; the base for Chandra bala, Tara bala, Sade Sati and transits here.
The Moon's nakshatra at birth; sets the Vimshottari balance and the Tara bala count.
A house of the chart, one of twelve areas of life counted from the Lagna.
A house diagram with cusps centred on the Lagna degree, so a planet near a boundary may shift house.
The lord of a house: the planet that rules the sign occupying that house.
The lord of a sign: Mars rules Mesha and Vrishchika, Venus Vrishabha and Tula, and so on.
A 'planet' of Jyotish: Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn and the nodes Rahu and Ketu.
Graha of the self and vitality; exalted in Mesha, debilitated in Tula, lord of Simha.
Graha of the mind and the tithi; exalted in Vrishabha, debilitated in Vrishchika, lord of Karka.
Graha of energy and effort; exalted in Makara, debilitated in Karka, lord of Mesha and Vrishchika.
Graha of speech and reasoning; exalted in Kanya, debilitated in Meena, lord of Mithuna and Kanya.
Graha of wisdom and growth; exalted in Karka, debilitated in Makara, lord of Dhanu and Meena.
Graha of relationships and comfort; exalted in Meena, debilitated in Kanya, lord of Vrishabha and Tula.
Graha of discipline and time; exalted in Tula, debilitated in Mesha, lord of Makara and Kumbha.
The Moon's north node, a shadow graha without a sign of its own; read with Saturn's friendships here.
The Moon's south node, always opposite Rahu; read with Mars's friendships here.
Rahu's averaged position (default here); the 'true' node wobbles around it by up to about 1.7°.
Sign 1 (Aries); fire, movable, ruled by Mars.
Sign 2 (Taurus); earth, fixed, ruled by Venus.
Sign 3 (Gemini); air, dual, ruled by Mercury.
Sign 4 (Karkata, the crab); water, movable, ruled by the Moon.
Sign 5 (Leo); fire, fixed, ruled by the Sun.
Sign 6 (Virgo); earth, dual, ruled by Mercury.
Sign 7 (Libra); air, movable, ruled by Venus.
Sign 8 (Scorpio); water, fixed, ruled by Mars.
Sign 9 (Sagittarius); fire, dual, ruled by Jupiter.
Sign 10 (Capricorn); earth, movable, ruled by Saturn. The Sun's entry here is Makar Sankranti.
Sign 11 (Aquarius); air, fixed, ruled by Saturn.
Sign 12 (Pisces); water, dual, ruled by Jupiter.
Nakshatra 1, 0°-13°20' Mesha; lord Ketu.
Nakshatra 2, 13°20'-26°40' Mesha; lord Venus.
Nakshatra 3, 26°40' Mesha to 10° Vrishabha; lord Sun. Karthigai Deepam is its day in Vrishchika's solar month.
Nakshatra 4, 10°-23°20' Vrishabha; lord Moon. Janmashtami prefers the midnight that holds Rohini.
Nakshatra 5, 23°20' Vrishabha to 6°40' Mithuna; lord Mars.
Nakshatra 6, 6°40'-20° Mithuna; lord Rahu.
Nakshatra 7, 20° Mithuna to 3°20' Karka; lord Jupiter.
Nakshatra 8, 3°20'-16°40' Karka; lord Saturn. Thaipusam is its day in Makara's solar month.
Nakshatra 9, 16°40'-30° Karka; lord Mercury.
Nakshatra 10, 0°-13°20' Simha; lord Ketu. Also the name of the lunar month Magha.
Nakshatra 11, 13°20'-26°40' Simha; lord Venus.
Nakshatra 12, 26°40' Simha to 10° Kanya; lord Sun.
Nakshatra 13, 10°-23°20' Kanya; lord Moon.
Nakshatra 14, 23°20' Kanya to 6°40' Tula; lord Mars.
Nakshatra 15, 6°40'-20° Tula; lord Rahu.
Nakshatra 16, 20° Tula to 3°20' Vrishchika; lord Jupiter.
Nakshatra 17, 3°20'-16°40' Vrishchika; lord Saturn.
Nakshatra 18, 16°40'-30° Vrishchika; lord Mercury. Also the lunar month Jyeshtha.
Nakshatra 19, 0°-13°20' Dhanu; lord Ketu.
Nakshatra 20, 13°20'-26°40' Dhanu; lord Venus.
Nakshatra 21, 26°40' Dhanu to 10° Makara; lord Sun. Onam (Thiruvonam) is Shravana's day, the next nakshatra.
Nakshatra 22, 10°-23°20' Makara; lord Moon. Onam is its day in Simha's solar month.
Nakshatra 23, 23°20' Makara to 6°40' Kumbha; lord Mars. Panchak begins in its Kumbha half.
Nakshatra 24, 6°40'-20° Kumbha; lord Rahu.
Nakshatra 25, 20° Kumbha to 3°20' Meena; lord Jupiter.
Nakshatra 26, 3°20'-16°40' Meena; lord Saturn.
Nakshatra 27, 16°40'-30° Meena; lord Mercury. Panchak ends with it.
A quarter of a nakshatra (3°20'); each pada is one navamsa sign.
The ninth-division chart (D9); each sign is split into nine parts of 3°20'.
A divisional chart; D1 is the main chart and D9 the navamsa.
A planet in the same sign in D1 and D9; counted as a strength.
The offset between tropical and sidereal zodiacs (about 24° today); Lahiri is the default, KP and Raman are options.
The Chitrapaksha ayanamsa adopted by the Indian calendar committee; the default here.
Exaltation: the sign where a planet is strongest (Sun in Mesha, Moon in Vrishabha, and so on).
Debilitation: the sign opposite a planet's exaltation, where it is weakest.
Own sign: a planet in a sign it rules.
A friend's sign by Parashara's natural friendships; read as supportive.
An enemy's sign by Parashara's natural friendships; read as uneasy.
A neutral planet's sign; neither friend nor enemy.
Combust: a planet within its orb of the Sun (Moon 12°, Mars 17°, Mercury 14°, Jupiter 11°, Venus 10°, Saturn 15°).
Retrograde: a planet apparently moving backwards through the zodiac, marked R in the chart.
A planetary period; the Vimshottari system gives each of nine planets a share of a 120-year cycle.
The 120-year dasha system seeded by the Moon's birth nakshatra and its lord.
The major period of a planet (6 to 20 years) in Vimshottari.
A sub-period inside a mahadasha; nine per mahadasha in the same planetary order.
The third level: a sub-sub-period inside an antardasha, lasting weeks to months.
Transit: a planet's present sign counted from the natal Moon; Saturn, Jupiter and Rahu are tracked here.
Saturn's roughly seven and a half years through the 12th, 1st and 2nd signs from the natal Moon.
Saturn's roughly two and a half years in the 4th (Kantaka) or 8th (Ashtama) sign from the natal Moon.
The day Moon's house from the birth Moon; 1, 3, 6, 7, 10 and 11 are read as favourable.
The day Moon in the 8th sign from the birth Moon, about two days a month; routine tasks today, new starts tomorrow.
The day nakshatra counted from the birth nakshatra in nine taras; 2, 4, 6, 8 and 9 are read as supportive.
Tara 1: the day nakshatra is the birth nakshatra or 10th/19th from it; read as mixed.
Tara 2 (2nd, 11th, 20th from the birth nakshatra); read as supportive.
Tara 3 (3rd, 12th, 21st); read as unsupportive for new starts.
Tara 4 (4th, 13th, 22nd); read as supportive.
Tara 5 (5th, 14th, 23rd); read as unsupportive for new starts.
Tara 6 (6th, 15th, 24th); read as supportive.
Tara 7 (7th, 16th, 25th); read as the least supportive tara.
Tara 8 (8th, 17th, 26th); read as supportive.
Tara 9 (9th, 18th, 27th); read as the most supportive tara.
Lunar month 1 (March-April); Chaitra Navratri, Ugadi, Gudi Padwa and Rama Navami fall in its Shukla paksha.
Lunar month 2 (April-May); Akshaya Tritiya and Buddha Purnima.
Lunar month 3 (May-June); Nirjala Ekadashi, Vat Savitri and Ganga Dussehra.
Lunar month 4 (June-July); Rath Yatra, Devshayani Ekadashi and Guru Purnima.
Lunar month 5 (July-August), also Sawan; Shravan Somvar, Hariyali Teej, Nag Panchami, Raksha Bandhan.
Lunar month 6 (August-September); Janmashtami, Hartalika Teej, Ganesh Chaturthi, Anant Chaturdashi.
Lunar month 7 (September-October); Pitru Paksha (Krishna), Sharad Navratri and Dussehra (Shukla).
Lunar month 8 (October-November); Karwa Chauth, Diwali, Chhath, Dev Uthani Ekadashi and Kartik Purnima.
Lunar month 9 (November-December), also Agahan; Vivah Panchami, Gita Jayanti, Dattatreya Jayanti.
Lunar month 10 (December-January); Saphala and Pausha Putrada Ekadashi, Pausha Purnima.
Lunar month 11 (January-February); Mauni Amavasya, Vasant Panchami, Ratha Saptami, Magha Purnima.
Lunar month 12 (February-March); Maha Shivaratri, Holika Dahan and Holi.
A birth anniversary observed by tithi (Hanuman, Narasimha, Parashurama, Mahavir Jayanti).
Worship with offerings, at home or in a temple; the app only shows timings, it sells nothing.
Vaishakha Shukla Tritiya, held good for any start; kept on its begin day when fewer than three muhurtas remain after sunrise.
The period before an eclipse during which rites are paused; not modelled by the engine in this version.
Observation-based calculation of planetary positions, as used here (astronomy-engine ephemeris).
The sage of the Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, source of the dignities, friendships and Vimshottari rules used here.
An 18th-century digest of festival and vrat timing rules; the source cited for most festival dates here.
Houses 1, 4, 7 and 10, the pillars of the chart; planets in them are read as prominent.
Houses 1, 5 and 9, the fortunate triangle of the chart.
Houses 6, 8 and 12, where planets are read as working through difficulty, debt, loss or retreat.
The lord of the Lagna sign; the planet a reader looks at first in a chart with a known birth time.
The rising sign on the eastern horizon at the birth moment, the ordinary meaning of Lagna.
Exchange: two planets each placed in the sign the other owns; graded by the houses involved.
The real lunar month of a name, as opposed to the inserted adhik month; tithi events are kept in the nija month.
The part of the first Vimshottari period remaining at birth, set by how far the Moon had travelled in its nakshatra.
A named planetary pattern in a birth chart (Gaja Kesari, Kemadruma, Mahapurusha ...); distinct from the panchang yoga.
Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon; weakened when Jupiter is combust or debilitated.
Five yogas: Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus or Saturn in own or exalted sign in a kendra from the Lagna.
A Moon with no planet (other than the Sun, Rahu, Ketu) in the signs on either side; cancelled by several bhanga rules.
Cancellation of a yoga or dosha by a classical condition; shown here as formed but cancelled, with the rule named.
All seven planets on one side of the Rahu-Ketu axis; the texts disagree about its reading and its reversed form.
The D2 divisional chart, each sign halved between the Sun and the Moon; read for resources.
The D3 divisional chart, each sign in three parts of ten degrees; read for siblings and effort.
The D10 divisional chart, each sign in ten parts; read for work and public standing.
The D30 divisional chart, each sign in five unequal parts ruled by the five visible planets; read for difficulty.
The D60 divisional chart, each sign in sixty parts of half a degree; the varga Parashara weights most.
Parashara's point system: benefic points (bindus) given to signs from eight reference points, summed per planet and in all.
One benefic point in Ashtakavarga; a sign holds 0-8 for one planet and about 15-40 in the total.
The per-planet Ashtakavarga table: bindus each sign receives for one planet.
The sum of the seven planets' Ashtakavarga tables; 337 bindus across the twelve signs.
A modern method using Placidus cusps, its own ayanamsa and sub-lords from the Vimshottari proportions.
A time-based house system with unequal cusps, used by KP; undefined above the polar circles.
The starting degree of a house in a cusp-based system such as Placidus; KP reads its sub-lord.
In KP, the Vimshottari lord of the unequal ninth-part of a nakshatra a point falls in; read as the decider of a cusp.
The Vimshottari lord of the nakshatra a point occupies; the middle of KP's three lords.
In KP, a planet linked to a house by occupation or ownership, graded A to D by star-lord and own placement.
KP's planets of the moment: lords of the rising Lagna, the Moon's position and the weekday.
Eight-heading matching of two birth Moons, 36 points in all: Varna, Vashya, Tara, Yoni, Graha Maitri, Gana, Bhakoot, Nadi.
A point in Ashtakoota matching; the total is a count of rules met out of 36, not a probability.
The one-point koota comparing the Moon signs' class grouping.
The two-point koota comparing the Moon signs' vashya groups (quadruped, human, water, wild, insect).
The four-point koota comparing the animal symbols of the two birth nakshatras.
The five-point koota comparing the natural friendship of the two Moon-sign lords.
The six-point koota comparing the deva, manushya or rakshasa gana of the two birth nakshatras.
The seven-point koota on the distance between the two Moon signs; exceptions when the lords are the same or friends.
The eight-point koota on the two nakshatras' nadi group; exceptions for a shared sign or shared nakshatra with different padas.
Mars in house 1, 2, 4, 7, 8 or 12 from the Lagna, Moon or Venus; six classical cancellations are checked and named.
A chosen time for an activity: windows that pass the kaals and the activity's tithi, nakshatra and weekday rules.
Entering a new home for the first time; one of the fourteen muhurat activities with its own tithi and nakshatra table.
The astronomical model that gives planetary positions for any instant; here astronomy-engine, run on the phone.
Positions measured from a fixed star point, as Jyotish uses; tropical position minus the ayanamsa.
Positions measured from the equinox, as the ephemeris gives them; the ayanamsa converts them to sidereal.
Rahu and Ketu at the Moon's actual crossings of the ecliptic, wobbling up to about 1.5 degrees around the mean node.
A chart cast for the moment a question is asked, at the place of asking; read for the question, not the birth.
